title: Best Virtual Assistants (2026): How to Hire One You Can Trust
description: How to hire a virtual assistant: what the package should include, how to brief tasks, what drives the price and the red flags to avoid.
intro: A virtual assistant can take repetitive work off your plate: email, scheduling, data entry, research, customer replies. The arrangement works when tasks are clearly written down and access is shared safely. It fails when instructions live only in your head or when an assistant is given your main passwords. This guide covers both.

faq.q: What tasks can a virtual assistant do?
faq.a: Common tasks include managing an inbox, booking meetings, data entry, online research, updating spreadsheets, customer service replies and simple social media posting. Tasks that follow clear steps are the easiest to hand over.

faq.q: How should I share access to my accounts?
faq.a: Create separate user accounts or use delegated access where the tool allows it, and share logins through a password manager rather than by message. Never share your main email or banking password, and remove access when the work ends.

faq.q: Should I pay per task or per hour?
faq.a: Per-task packages suit one-off jobs with a clear result. Hourly or monthly arrangements suit ongoing work. Either way, agree on what is included and how time is reported.

faq.q: How do I handle time zones?
faq.a: A different time zone can be an advantage, with work done while you sleep, but agree on overlap hours for questions and on how quickly messages will be answered.

faq.q: What if the assistant handles customer data?
faq.a: Share only what the task needs, keep data in your own tools rather than theirs, and check the privacy rules that apply to your business. A confidentiality agreement is sensible for sensitive work.
